messages.subject: Comparing absolute amplitude across different microphone enclosures
messages.subject_clean: Comparing absolute amplitude across different microphone enclosures
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am testing how different enclosures affect the AudioMoth microphone sensitivity. I conducted multiple playbacks with the microphone facing different orientations (0 = facing the microphone, 60, 120, 180, 240, 300). The playback file has 1s long tones that go from 1kHz to 12kHz, a sweep that goes from 1-12kHz, and two chipping sparrow songs.

I am trying to analyze the tones individually. In Audacity, when I do a plot spectrum analysis I get relative amplitude values that demonstrate the differences in microphone sensitivity across the different microphone orientations. However when I use the meanspec() function in seewave, the tones have the same amplitude regardless of the microphone orientation, even when I set  norm = FALSE to get absolute values. What can I do to get these absolute values?

tone_all_000 = readWave("amoth_naked_000_trial01.wav",
                from = 11.25,
                to = 11.75,
                units = "seconds",
                correction = "none",
                PMF = FALSE,
                flim = c(0,12),
                norm = FALSE)

tone_all_180 = readWave("amoth_naked_180_trial01.wav",
                        from = 11.25,
                        to = 11.75,
                        units = "seconds",
              correction = "none",
                PMF = FALSE,
                flim = c(0,12),
                norm = FALSE)

Thanks and kind regards,

Meelyn

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Change dBref seawater
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Please include this information in the next package description. I have spent an embarrassing amount of time trying to double check this reference value.  Also, is it upper peak, peak to peak, RMS, etc. I believe these values are p2p.  Cheers!

On Tuesday, March 24, 2020 at 7:30:25 AM UTC+1 Jérôme SUEUR wrote:
> Hello,
>
> The reference pressure value is indeed 20 microPa = 20*10e-6 Pa = 2*10e-5=0.00002 Pa
>
> So yes you should be able to use 1*10^-6.
>
> HTH
>
> Jerome
>
> De: "SA" <sofy...@gmail.com>
> À: "seewave GROUP" <see...@googlegroups.com>
> Envoyé: Vendredi 20 Mars 2020 12:08:23
> Objet: [seewave] Change dBref seawater
>
> Hi,
> I'm working on underwater soundscape and was looking into changing the reference pressure to 1microPa.
> The thing is, when I check the help file for the spec function for instance (or even the package vignette), and there is not much information on using other values...
>
> In air, the reference pressure value is 20microPa.
>
> Please forgive the ignorance, but the value recommended for air is 20*10e-5 and if this value is in Pascals it corresponds to 0.002 Pascals, which is 2000 microPa, not 20, right?
> I get a bit confused as to how this estimate was done and which units are being used.
> If everything is in Pascal, then I should easily use 1*10^-6 but am afraid of trusting values without knowing what is going on with the calculations suggested.
>
>
> Any help with this would be appreciated.
>
> Cheers,
> SA

messages.subject: Multi-channel plots
messages.body_plain:
Has anyone had any success plotting multiple channels in one image? I have a four channel wave file that I would like to display, and am having issues getting it to work properly.  I have tried:

par(mfrow=c(4,1))
spectro(wav1,scale=FALSE, wl=256, flimd = c(0.01,3), grid= FALSE, ovlp = 95, osc = TRUE,dBref = 1*10^-6,palette=reverse.gray.colors.1 , collevels = seq(50,125,2))

spectro(wav2, scale=FALSE,  wl=256, flimd = c(0.01,3),grid= FALSE, ovlp = 95,axisX=FALSE,tlab='',osc = TRUE, dBref = 1*10^-6,palette=reverse.gray.colors.1, collevels = seq(50,150,5) )

spectro(wav3,channel = 1,scale=FALSE, wl=256, grid= FALSE, flimd = c(0.01,3),axisX=FALSE,tlab='',ovlp = 95, osc = TRUE, dBref = 1*10^-6,palette=reverse.gray.colors.1, collevels = seq(50,150,5) )

spectro(wav3,channel = 2,scale = FALSE, wl=256, grid= FALSE, flimd = c(0.01,3),axisX=FALSE,tlab='', ovlp = 95, osc = TRUE, dBref = 1*10^-6,palette=reverse.gray.colors.1, collevels = seq(50,150,5) )
title(main="Tyra East 2A, Channel 2 Low Sensitivity")

I have merged them all into one wav object and tried to plot that as well.

m1A <- wav1@left
m2A <- wav2@left
m3A <- wav3@left
m4A <- wav3@right

# combine the four files into one multi-channel file

WavPDex <- WaveMC(data = list(m1A, m2A, m3A, m4A), samp.rate = 6000, bit = 16, pcm = TRUE)

## Hot_theme_grid shamelessly borrowed from Joshua Flickinger, spectro(2018) winner.

ggspectro(wave = WavPDex, f = Wav...@samp.rate, ovlp=90,wl=512)+
  geom_raster(aes(fill=amplitude), hjust = 0, vjust = 0, interpolate = F)+
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = hot_colors, name = "Amplitude \n (dB)", na.value = "transparent", limits = c(-60,0))+
  hot_theme_grid

These attempts only return one channel. Is there a command that I am missing to display multiple channel plots?

Cheers,
Emily

messages.body_plain:
FYI, This is how I am getting it to work now. It doesn't look as clean as I'd like it to, so I am still working out the details.

spec1=ggspectro(wave = wav1, f =  wav1 @samp.rate, channel = 2, ovlp=90,wl=512, dBref = 1*10^-6, osc = TRUE)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(from = 0, to = 5, by=1),  labels = khz_formatter)+

  geom_raster(aes(fill=amplitude), hjust = 0, vjust = 0, interpolate = F)+

  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = hot_colors, name = "Amplitude \n (dB)", na.value = "transparent", limits = c(20,130))+
  annotate(geom='text',x=3,y=4.75,label= 'Wav1', color ='white', size=4)+
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill="black"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill="white"),
        panel.border = element_rect(linetype = "solid", fill = NA, color = "black"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        #axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none",
        #text=element_text(size=13)
        )

spec2=ggspectro(wave = wav2, f =  wav2 @samp.rate, channel = 2, ovlp=90,wl=512, dBref = 1*10^-6, osc = TRUE)+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(from = 0, to = 5, by=1),  labels = khz_formatter)+

  geom_raster(aes(fill=amplitude), hjust = 0, vjust = 0, interpolate = F)+

  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = hot_colors, name = "Amplitude \n (dB)", na.value = "transparent", limits = c(20,130))+
  annotate(geom='text',x=3,y=4.75,label= 'Wav2', color ='white', size=4)+
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill="black"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill="white"),
        panel.border = element_rect(linetype = "solid", fill = NA, color = "black"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        #axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none",
        #text=element_text(size=13)
        )

#etc...

gA=ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(spec1))
gB=ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build( spec2 ))
gC=ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build( spec3 ))
gD=ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build( spec4 ))

maxWidth = grid::unit.pmax(gA$widths, gB$widths, gC$widths, gD$widths)
gA$widths <- as.list(maxWidth)
gB$widths <- as.list(maxWidth)
gC$widths <- as.list(maxWidth)
gD$widths <- as.list(maxWidth)
grid.newpage()
grid.arrange(gA, gB, gC,gD, ncol = 1, left='Frequency (kHz)', bottom = 'Time (s)')

This still isn't exactly what I am looking for, and would be very open to advice!

-Emily

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: Multi-channel plots
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emily,

I haven't tried this specifically, but have you tried the patchwork package for combining plots? https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com/articles/patchwork.html

I find it much more straightforward than grid.arrange.

I think the syntax you'd like would be:
library(patchwork)

spec1 = ggspectro(...)
...
spec1 / spec2 / spec3

An alternative would be to use spectro to extract the frequency/amp/time data into a data frame, combine all channels into one data frame and then facet_wrap() by channel. https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/facet_wrap.html

You add the geom like you have below (soemthing like that, anyway I've forgotten the specifies), but it's definitely doable. This code isn't the right one, but
ggplot(data = spec, aes(x = time, y = freq, fill = amplitude) +
 geom_raster() +
 facet_wrap(~channel, ncol = 1)

Hope these give you some ideas, take care!

Steffi
